paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2006 - A Framework to Provide Trust and Incentive in CROWN Grid for Dynamic Resource Management
title: A Framework to Provide Trust and Incentive in CROWN Grid for Dynamic Resource Management
motivation: Grid resources are depleted by selfish users taking free rides; existing soft incentive cannot satisfy providers' desire for benefit.
problem_framing: Combine soft incentive (reputation) and hard incentive (price) to achieve trust-incentive compatibility in dynamic grid resource allocation.
key_insight: Users gain more resources only if they share more AND possess higher trust; the mechanism integrates price, trust, and incentive as complementary levers.
method_signature: TIM framework with four models (Child, Club, Bids, Trust) using weighted voting for admission control and price-based allocation.
evaluation_criteria: Allocation ratio, job completion time, system completion ratio, aggregated resource utilization, revenue under malicious attacks.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Hard incentive alone fails: 'wealthy nodes are not always with higher degree reputation. Simply considering bid price cannot satisfy security concerns.'
evidence_for_taste: wealthy nodes are not always with higher degree reputation
The more resources a node provides, the higher degree of trust a node has
the provision ratio of node 3 (60%) is less than node 1 (90%), but node 3 has a higher trust value
Club considering both benefit and security factors (α=0.5) obtains more revenue
the revenue of Club2 without TIM is suffering much more than Club1 with TIM
thinking_moves: Merge two previously separate incentive paradigms (soft vs hard) by finding their complementary strengths
Admit that economic rationality alone fails security requirements — wealthy ≠ trustworthy
Use risk-degree parameter α to dynamically balance economic gain vs security
Model trust as a compounding function (1-(1-T2)^T1) rather than simple average
Replace Smale's continuous equilibrium with discrete iteration for practical grid deployment
cites_own_work: Liu et al. 2004 on Location-Aware Topology Matching
Huai et al. 2005 on Distributed Access Control in CROWN Groups
